title: Ellipses and Hyperbolas with Center (h, k)
seo_title: Precalculus Ellipses and Hyperbolas Worksheets (TEKS P.3H, P.3I)
standard_text: P.3H use the characteristics of an ellipse to write the equation of an ellipse with center (h, k); P.3I use the characteristics of a hyperbola to write the equation of a hyperbola with center (h, k)
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on ellipses and hyperbolas for Texas TEKS P.3H and P.3I: vertices, foci, writing equations with center (h, k) and asymptotes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Ellipse: c² = a² − b². Hyperbola: c² = a² + b².
key_sub: a is the distance from the center to a vertex.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Ellipse with center (h, k): (x − h)2a2 + (y − k)2b2 = 1 (horizontal major axis). The bigger denominator is a2. c2 = a2 − b2.
  • Hyperbola: (x − h)2a2 − (y − k)2b2 = 1 opens left and right. c2 = a2 + b2.
  • a is the distance from the center to a vertex; c is the distance to a focus.
  • Asymptotes of a horizontal hyperbola: y − k = ±ba(x − h).

Examples

Example

Vertices (−1, 2) and (7, 2), foci (−2, 2) and (8, 2)

Center (3, 2), a = 4, c = 5

Hyperbola: b2 = 25 − 16 = 9

Answer: (x − 3)216 − (y − 2)29 = 1

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
a2 under the wrong variablea goes with the axis through the vertices.
c2 = a2 + b2 for an ellipseEllipse: minus. Hyperbola: plus.
The wrong signs for the centerCenter (3, −2) gives (x − 3) and (y + 2).

faq.q: How can I tell an ellipse from a hyperbola?
faq.a: Ellipse: plus between the terms. Hyperbola: minus.

faq.q: Which way does a hyperbola open?
faq.a: Toward the variable whose term is positive.
